claims.text: The starting material is an as-solidified AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar microstructure.
The starting alloy has suboptimal strength and plasticity for fastener applications.
The proposed intervention is solutionizing at approximately 1100°C, aging at 700°C for 10 hours under inert atmosphere with an intermediate quench, and then air cooling.
An intermediate quench during aging will prevent or limit precipitate over-aging and coarsening.
The heat treatment will produce a fine nanoscale dispersion of ordered B2 precipitates.
The B2 precipitates will preferentially form along the lamellar interfaces.
Fine B2 precipitates will impede dislocation motion through precipitation hardening.
The proposed B2 precipitate network will retard creep deformation.
The proposed precipitate network will stabilize the microstructure against corrosive degradation.
The treated alloy will have at least approximately 10% higher yield strength than the untreated lamellar alloy.
The treated alloy will retain more plasticity than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will exhibit a lower room-temperature creep rate than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will have better corrosion resistance than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will have better fatigue resistance under cyclic and high-temperature conditions than the untreated alloy.
The performance improvement is expected to remain applicable at operating temperatures up to 500°C.
The untreated fine-lamellar alloy has limited creep resistance and corrosion performance.
The kinetics of B2 precipitate formation and growth under the proposed aging and quenching schedule are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The treatment is described as a 10-hour aging treatment with a quench introduced midway and followed by air cooling, but no reheating or return to 700°C is specified after the intermediate quench. Thus, the full 10-hour aging schedule and the stated post-quench cooling sequence are operationally incompatible or ambiguous.
